Hi Daniel — great to connect. 45 minutes sounds about right. We can do Tue 6/8 at 10:30 PT or Wed 6/9 at 11:00 PT. Which works better for you and Sally?

Quick answers up front to help prep:
- Scope: by default we include hosted API and Dedicated; Private/VPC on-prem requires slightly different evidence (network diagrams, customer-managed keys) — we’ll confirm during call.
- Log types we can provide: auth, admin, api_access, request-trace (application traces), and infrastructure (host) logs. Format: newline-delimited JSON or syslog text.
- CAIQ/SIG: Olga will lead the SIG/CAIQ answers; typical turnaround for a first draft is 5–7 business days for the baseline responses, shorter for clarifications.
- Secure drop: we prefer a scoped GCS/S3 share or encrypted Drive link; we can accept temporary signed URLs for initial uploads.

I attached a short intake agenda and a sample log schema to this reply to make the call efficient. On internal side I’ll loop Marissa for log sample preparation and Olga for CAIQ.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SOC 2 intake and log sample request — meeting notes and actions

Hi Daniel & Sally — thanks for the productive call today. Notes and agreed actions below. Please reply with any corrections; otherwise we’ll proceed to the timestamps below.

Meeting summary (45 min):
- Scope: Crestline wants SOC 2 coverage for production-hosted API and Dedicated pools used for their workloads. Private/VPC customers were discussed and will require additional customer-supplied network diagrams; not in immediate scope.
- Log coverage: Redwood can provide auth, api_access, request-trace, and infra logs. Format: newline JSON preferred.
- Retention: hosted API logs retained by default 90 days; Dedicated customers can configure up to 365 days with a retention policy/contract addendum. We flagged retention differences for scoping (Daniel to confirm required retention for Crestline).
- KMS: For Private/VPC, key custody is customer-managed; for Dedicated/Hosted, Redwood manages KMS but we can provide key rotation policies and KMS attestations as evidence.
- PII: We confirmed token hashes are persisted, raw token values are never logged. Authentication identifiers are hashed; we will include a redaction note in the sample README.

Action items and owners (due dates):
1) Marissa Cole (Redwood) — upload three redacted log samples (auth, api_access, infra) to Crestline Drive folder. Due: 2027-06-11 EOD. (Attachment: log_sample_schema.txt)
2) Olga Petrov (Redwood) — deliver CAIQ baseline and flagged controls; first draft due: 2027-06-16. (Attachment: SOC2_scoping_matrix.xlsx will capture control mappings)
3) Daniel / Crestline — confirm required retention window for scope decision and confirm whether Private/VPC should be included. Due: 2027-06-10.
4) Karthik Iyer (Redwood) — provide KMS attestation and typical rotation schedule (to be attached to CAIQ responses). Due: 2027-06-15.

Attachments included: Redwood_SIG_Intake_Agenda.pdf; SOC2_scoping_matrix.xlsx; log_sample_schema.txt

Next meeting: tentative follow-up the week of 2027-06-21 to review CAIQ draft and sample logs (we’ll propose times after Crestline confirms retention).

Thanks all,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
